title: Owner decision log
purpose: A review/export surface for current suggestions, with original alternatives and dated execution history. Owner choices are never fabricated; autonomous low-risk publication work is separately recorded.

policy.name: adopt-after-silence
policy.text: A suggestion whose recommended path is reversible, low-risk, and does not depend on a fact only an Amazon account holder can supply is treated as pre-approved: the next agent pass implements it and records what it did on this page. Everything else holds until the owner picks. This exists because the brief says no manual input is required of the owner, while also requiring that a human reviews suggestions before changes - so the review has a default outcome rather than a veto that blocks the work.
policy.scope_limit: Silence never authorises: spending money, registering a domain, contacting Amazon or a brand on the owner's behalf, publishing an Amazon-served price or star rating, changing a compliance posture, deleting another session's committed evidence, or asserting any product fact the repository has flagged as unverified. Anything in that class waits, on this page, with its reason.
policy.rule_applied: auto-adopt requires: an option letter the suggestion recommends; that option marked reversible; that option's risk 'none' or 'low'; and no blocking question in state 'unknowable'. The four tests are computed from data/suggestions.json and data/questions.json at build time, so the table on the page cannot claim a default its own data does not support.
policy.recording: An executed default is recorded in `implemented`, never in `choices`. A pass that adds a row to `choices` is inventing an owner instruction; a pass that changes data without recording it in `implemented` is the same failure in the other direction.

how_to_return_a_choice: Pick the path on decision-log.html. The page stores it in this browser so a second visit shows the same answer.
Press 'Copy decision record' (or 'Download decision-log.json') and send the text back in any session, or commit it over this file.

The next agent pass reads data/decision-log.json before it reads suggestions.html's defaults, records what it implemented, and marks the row. Anything you did not pick keeps the default this page shows today.
choices_note: Empty at publication, deliberately. An owner decision is a fact about a person's intent, and no agent session may record one on their behalf - that is the difference between a default and a fabricated instruction. Rows appear here only after a choice is actually made, and each one carries its date.

implemented.what: Computed the 'start here' triage from the registers' own blocker fields and published it on decision-log.html, above the register: each row's downstream count is the transitive size of its 'blocks' arrays across data/suggestions.json and data/questions.json, so the ranking regenerates with the registers instead of going stale (the F63/F52 defect class this repository keeps finding).
implemented.why_allowed: SG-26's own default: option A, reversible, risk low, blocked only by questions in state 'missing' rather than 'unknowable'. The standing rule on this page authorises exactly that.

implemented.what: The article set ships an RSS feed (feed.xml, 21 items after the cluster pass), regenerated on every build and linked from every page footer, so returning readers and aggregators learn about new guides without any account, cookie or third-party script.
implemented.why_allowed: The feed matches the site's no-cookie privacy posture exactly; SG-28 named the feed as the reader-loop mechanism and it was already shipped, so only its register state was stale.

implemented.what: Four reader-intent clusters (choose, spec, live, trust) file all 21 articles one-to-one via data/clusters.json; clusters.html publishes the map, article pages link cluster siblings and their hub, and check_clusters() fails the build on unfiled, duplicated, missing, empty or invalid-hub records - verified by two deliberate fault injections.
implemented.why_allowed: SG-35 recommended clustering as the path to owning commercial queries; no row value needed a new claim - cluster membership is an editorial filing of existing, sourced articles.

implemented.what: A privacy-preserving outbound-click counter (EV-01 page_view, EV-02 outbound_product_click, EV-03 guide_completed, EV-04 comparison_table_viewed, EV-05 reported_order) ships with its client committed and emitted on every page, but data/config.json holds no endpoint and data/analytics-plan.json keeps collection disabled, so the script sends nothing; self-hosted endpoint sources (PHP and Cloudflare Worker) are committed and undeployed, and check_analytics_consistency() fails the build on any unsafe configuration.
implemented.why_allowed: SG-08 allowed option B only with an updated disclosure on the same commit - done (privacy_html() and measurement.html state exactly what is and is not collected). The campaign ledger stays empty; no conversion or revenue figure is published.

implemented.what: The front page now opens with the three product cards — capacity, the brand's own list price with the policy reason no Amazon price appears beside it, a 'Best for' row and a 'Check first' row — and the metric tiles moved under the comparison table. Order only: no value changed, and the disclosure band and the paid-link labels stayed where the compliance guards expect them.
implemented.why_allowed: The row's own recommendation is option A: effort S-M, risk low or none, reversible, and blocked by nothing in state 'unknowable'. The standing rule on this page authorises implementing that and recording it here. No claim about conversion is made anywhere in the change, because no click data exists (Q-30).

implemented.what: Every product page gained the same two merchandising rows as a decision block above the fold, generated by merch_pair() from the product's own sourced spec and flag rows, plus a compact sponsored CTA on the front-page card. Option B of that row ('who should not buy this') is deliberately NOT implemented: it is advice rather than a quotation, so it waits for you.
implemented.why_allowed: The row's own recommendation is option A: effort S-M, risk low or none, reversible, and blocked by nothing in state 'unknowable'. The standing rule on this page authorises implementing that and recording it here. No claim about conversion is made anywhere in the change, because no click data exists (Q-30).

implemented.what: Mobile-first chrome: one clamp() type scale per heading level, a 44 px minimum hit area on every interactive control, a bottom-anchored comparison bar on reader pages only (hidden on desktop, in print and while the footer is on screen), and a hint under any table genuinely wider than the viewport. The bar carries no purchase button — option B of that row stays open until a click counter exists.
implemented.why_allowed: The row's own recommendation is option A: effort S-M, risk low or none, reversible, and blocked by nothing in state 'unknowable'. The standing rule on this page authorises implementing that and recording it here. No claim about conversion is made anywhere in the change, because no click data exists (Q-30).

implemented.what: Reconciled the actual browser client, Python collector, two event registers, privacy notice and enablement guards around page_view, outbound_click, article_engagement, comparison_interaction and the operator-only affiliate_report_import. Retired the incompatible PHP/Worker raw-event examples with HTTP 410. Actual JavaScript fixture payloads pass the Python validator; no production event or account report was created. The 2026-11-17 executed entry above describes the historical implementation, not the repaired protocol.
implemented.why_allowed: Bug repair within the existing five-event scope and accurate privacy disclosures, without choosing a host, spending money, enabling collection or asserting account evidence. All deployment/privacy flags remain false.

implemented.what: Moved the canonical publication to a format-led shelf and journal, compact buyer navigation, one native owner/evidence workspace and a comprehensive footer. The Associates statement is beneath the masthead, as explicitly requested, and repeated in the footer. Metrics no longer lead the front page. Clearly labelled generic AI-generated preparation/food scenes contain no promoted appliance or asserted recipe result; schematic format drawings are not product photographs. The rejected generated-appliance candidate is not published.
implemented.why_allowed: The user explicitly requested a useful publication rather than an audit dashboard. These reversible local presentation changes do not settle the product-photography permission question, alter any intended identity or imply a measured conversion gain. No owner choice was fabricated.

implemented.path: Documented-use block retained; stale offer-like snapshots demoted
implemented.what: Product pages now lead with the documented format/use, the model caveat, an explicitly sponsored link and the sourced specifications. Dated manufacturer pricing and commission uncertainty are retained in expandable publisher evidence, not used as live prices or a rating-based recommendation. Brand review widgets are not front-page or product-page social proof. Full values remain in the dataset.
implemented.why_allowed: Reversible reader presentation and removal of unsupported comparative/probabilistic copy, not a product superiority claim, price API activation or invented testing experience.

implemented.what: The front page is now a buying guide: a hero that asks which shape fits the reader's kitchen, the three machines with capacity, footprint, temperature, the brand's list price and one thing to check, a sponsored Amazon button beside a disclosure line on each card, the season pair, and six buyer-question guides. The working pages sit behind one link group, 'Behind the site', in the sidebar and the footer.
implemented.why_allowed: Option A is the row's recommendation, marked reversible with low risk, and its only blocking question (Q-01) is in state 'missing', not 'unknowable'. No price from Amazon, no rating and no popularity claim was added: the list price is the brand's own, cited per card.

implemented.what: Navigation labels reviewed and reduced to three sidebar groups: Shop, The three machines, and a collapsed 'Behind the site' group that opens on working pages. The footer repeats Shop and Behind the site on every page. check_desk_nav() fails the build if a working page drops out of both.
implemented.why_allowed: Option A is the row's recommendation, reversible, low risk, and blocked by nothing. Where the working pages should finally live is left open as SG-49.

implemented_note: Rows a pass implemented without waiting for the owner, under the adopt-after-silence rule, each naming the path it took and why the rule allowed it. This is not the owner's decision list — choices[] stays owner-only and empty until a person fills it — and it exists so a default never looks like an instruction from someone who never gave one. A pass that implements something and does not record it here has broken the rule it used.

execution_updates.what: PUB-1 publication, source corrections, truthful authorship, RSS-only reader loop, cadence plan and native Workspace implementation. This is an agent execution record, not an owner choice or an account/production approval. Current partial/gated states override old effort/done fields.

Execution record for pass 15, not an owner choice. SG-43: the fortnightly cadence was spent on exactly one new guide (TP-22 → articles/probe-in-an-air-fryer.html), the kill rule was applied to a second candidate (TP-19 recorded as considered and held, with the cadence limit and its Q-20 gate both named on the topic row), and the new row carries published_at: null rather than a backfilled date. SG-51: executed only in part — the live Program Policies page was re-read the same day and three requirement rows were added with verbatim quotes and today's read date (C19, C20, C21), while the 14 April 2026 change notice itself could not be fetched (two failed attempts), so its other three items are registered as a re-read task and an open flag (F109) instead of being quoted as policy text. No path on any other row was treated as pre-approved by this pass.
